questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose NUS due to it being in a English speaking country, warm weather, centrally located in South East Asia, and finally a good academic reputation

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I recommend trying to study abroad. Singapore is a great location to try a good but also different way of university life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine. You receive a guide with different to-do's. Be aware of hidden waits in processes (i.e. waiting 3 days to get your profile picture approved etc.), so don't do everything last minute!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You receive a online guide on how to get to your accommodation (if living on campus) and how to get select courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
- Dormitories (houses and halls) <- I recommend! It's easier to meet locals through social arrangements
- Shared apartments

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Only halls have a compulsory meal plan. Most on-campus housing have a kitchen but the level of utensils vary a lot. I don’t recommend cooking, as food courts are cheap and okay varied.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Try to secure housing in the 1. round. I believe Utown is easiest, but PGP is also fine.
There is cleaning services in halls and houses ;)
Also AC is not guaranteed!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't have AC... None of my clothes got mould, but I was lucky

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You have to apply to each course and no course can overlap in your time table! 
Recommend finding alternatives to your courses (and alternatives to the alternatives...).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3 out of 4 classes I wanted. I couldn't get a very relevant finance course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the guide and don't do everything last minute

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took all 3000-level courses. The level is about 2nd year at UCPH. I heard 4000-level can be quite hard (master level almost).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It felt very much like high school in terms of teaching style. Many courses had mandatory attendance, weekly quizzes, assignment etc. 
A lot of focus on computational part of math, and not a lot of focus on theory. Most of the difficulty in exams stemmed from having to many small questions in very short time. All exams were closed book as well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Differential equations
Mathematical modelling
Operation research I (easy)
Money and Banking (easy)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mathematical modelling is a very strange math course. More about the "vibe" of modelling then actually doing hardcore modelling.

Housing DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Try to save, so you can travel.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food at food courts is only cost 25-30 kr for a meal

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go join a club! They have so many different clubs!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything. I did a lot of swimming in their swimming pools.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go travel in south east asia! Both during and after the semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
You have to reach out first. Many locals are quite shy. 
Most of your friends will be with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really. Perhaps having to do small quizzes all the time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open minded
You need to love chicken and rice - it's 90% of all meals...
Take time to enjoy other cultures - try to travel a lot!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Traveling afterwards! The semester ends in start december

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing friends and family

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
